items.title: Derived adic completion agrees with usual completion for finite modules tensored with a flat module
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors

items.difficulty_reason: Let I be an ideal in a Noetherian ring A. The lemma asserts two things: if M is a finite A-module and N is a flat A-module, then the derived I-adic completion of M tensor_A N is the usual I-adic completion of M tensor_A N; and if M is finite and f in A, then the derived I-adic completion of M_f is the usual I-adic completion of M_f (source lines 27317-27328). The proof introduces the notation M^wedge for the derived completion and lim M/I^nM for the usual completion, and assumes M is finite (proof lines 27330-27332). The key input is that the system Tor^A_i(M, A/I^n) is pro-zero for i > 0 (proof lines 27333-27335). Since Tor_i^A(M tensor_A N, A/I^n) equals Tor_i^A(M, A/I^n) tensor_A N by flatness of N, the same pro-zero statement holds for the tensored system (proof lines 27336-27338). The computation statement for the Noetherian case then shows that R lim ((M tensor_A N) tensor^L_A A/I^n) has cohomology only in degree 0, given by the usual completion lim (M tensor_A N)/I^n(M tensor_A N), which proves (1) (proof lines 27339-27342). Part (2) follows from (1) and the identification M_f = M tensor_A A_f, using that A_f is flat (proof line 27343). The non-routine content is the transfer of the pro-zero property across the flat base change and the recognition that the degree-0 cohomology of the derived limit is exactly the usual completion.
